tagline: Not a rulebook. A machine for meaning, and you already know how to run it.

epigraph.text: 'When I use a word,' Humpty Dumpty said, in rather a scornful tone, 'it means just what I choose it to mean—neither more nor less.'

art.note: The council decided to keep the strict grid and iron-gall marginalia, using capillary feathering to make the hand feel pressed into the paper.

writers.note: The voice is iron-gall and capillary: precise, handmade, and argumentative, entering through the reader's own grammar instincts.

nuggets.hook: One verb can turn a list into a sentence.
nuggets.body: Nouns, verbs, and adjectives are not labels; they are workers. Put the verb in charge and the sentence gets a direction.
Grammar rules keep clauses from colliding. When two ideas snap together, the reader knows who is doing what to whom.

nuggets.hook: A dash can make a sentence hold its breath.
nuggets.body: Punctuation is the traffic control of the page. A dash can pause, a comma can turn, and a semicolon can wait politely for the next thought.

nuggets.hook: Can a rule be guilty if everyone already breaks it?
nuggets.body: Descriptive grammar records what speakers already do. Prescriptive grammar asks what speakers should do, and the courtroom is where the two meet.
